resources.title: OH CMLL List (Anto's OH CMLL)
resources.author: Anto Kam (Rouxles). The sheet has no byline. Attribution comes from the rouxcubing.com label "Anto's OH CMLL", and YouTube oEmbed shows all 55 linked alg videos belong to the channel "Rouxles [Anto]" (@Rouxles). Case images are served from rouxl.es (formerly rouxles.github.io).
resources.level: intermediate to advanced (OH Roux solvers learning or refining full 1-look CMLL); this is the reference OH CMLL sheet that rouxcubing.com embeds and tutorial.rouxers.com /intermediate/cmll.html links to
resources.summary: A Google Sheet with 10 tabs: Info, one tab per corner-orientation (OCLL) group (O, H, PI, U, T, S, AS, L), and a hidden 'template' tab. It holds a full 1-look OH CMLL set: 42 cases and about 124 algorithms, written for left-hand OH, so the algs use R/U/F/r/f moves. A cell comment tells the solver to use the left index finger to push the UBL corner for L moves. Each group tab uses the same grid. Row 1 holds the case slot numbers 1-6; O uses only slots 3 and 6, and H uses 1, 2, 3 and 6. Row 2 gives the pattern name. Row 3 has an =IMAGE() formula that builds the case picture URL as rouxl.es/images/333/cmll/<Group><slot>.png. From row 4 down, each column lists the main alg first, then alternatives, each with its pre-AUF in brackets. Pattern names: O = Adjacent Swap / Diagonal Swap. H = Columns / Row / Column / Rows. Pi, AS and S use Right/Left Bar, Back/Forward Slash, X Checkerboard and Columns. U and T use Front/Back Row, Rows, Columns and Bars. L = Pure / Front Commutator / Good / Best / Back Commutator / Diagonal. The Info tab says italic algs are not main algs: they are alternatives used to influence LSE edge orientation (16 italic algs). 55 algs are HYPERLINKs to short demo videos on the Rouxles YouTube channel, titled by case id (for example 'Pi1 1', 'Pi1 2'). Every one of the 42 cases has at least one video, and 13 cases have a second one for an alternative alg. The algs are OH-specific: z rotations with D moves, wide moves, and cell comments on fingertricks ('Table R2' table abuse; the left-index push for L/L'). The hidden template tab is an older layout with 42 VisualCube (cubing.net) plan-view images at stage=cmll. Saved: CSV per tab, the xlsx export, the htmlview, an all-tabs text dump with style and comment markers, and the oEmbed titles of the 55 videos.

resources.title: Sevilz' OH CMLL (file title 'Sevilzww OH CMLL')
resources.author: Sevilz (YouTube @sevilzww). The Info tab also says 'Subscribe to Zhouheng Sun', which reads as a shout-out rather than a byline.
resources.level: advanced (OH Roux solvers optimising CMLL alg choice, EO effects and move counts)
resources.summary: A Google Sheet on the same template as Anto's: the same tab ids, the same rouxl.es =IMAGE() case pictures and the same hidden VisualCube 'template' tab. Tabs: Info, O, H, PI, U, S, AS, L, T, plus a 'CMLL Statistics' tab. It covers all 42 CMLL cases with 56 algs, written for left-hand OH (R/U/F-based). Info gives the conventions. Top alg = main alg. Bold = EO-preserving: the alg does not change edge orientation, so use it only when all edges are already oriented (2 algs). Underlined = an alg for angle coverage, meaning it executes the case from another AUF (11 algs). Info also jokes 'Dont use my algs unless you really think my turning is better than anto's turning'. Every alg except the two O algs has an embedded EO/EP effect diagram (54 PNGs, 300x453). The diagrams come from badochov's CMLL Visualiser. They show the U-face case corners plus the six LSE edges; a light-blue highlight marks an edge that will flip, and an arrow shows where it goes ('flipping first, arrows second'). The CMLL Statistics tab gives each case (Skip, O3, O6, H1-H4, Pi1-6, U1-6, S1-6, As1-6, L1-6, T1-6) a probability (2/81 for most cases; 1/81 for H1 and H4; 1/162 for O6 and for the skip). It also gives the main alg's STM, computed by a REGEXREPLACE formula that strips AUFs, rotations, primes and 2s, then the expected pre-AUF (0, 0.5 or 0.75), then a probability-weighted cost. Totals: average 10.5 STM, 0.63 pre-AUF, 11.20 weighted expected moves. Per-subset averages range from L at 9.54 to H at 12.75. Cell comments on the O algs name OH U2 fingertrick variants ('feido U2', 'beido'). Case-name quirk: the U tab labels slot 1 'Back Row' and slot 6 'Front Row', the reverse of Anto's sheet, even though both use the same images (U1.png, U6.png). Saved: CSV per tab, the xlsx, the htmlview, an all-tabs dump with bold/underline markers, and the 54 extracted EO diagrams in sevilz-media/ (named by tab and cell).

resources.level: beginner (first CMLL method, before full CMLL)
resources.summary: A small Google Sheet with 2 visible tabs and a hidden VisualCube 'template' tab. 'Orientation' lists 7 corner-orientation cases in 3 groups, labelled by the number of oriented corners. Group 0 is H and Pi (pictured as H1 and Pi1). Group 1 is Sune and Antisune (S1, plus an embedded AS image). Group 2 is U, T and L (U6, T5, plus an embedded L image). Each case has a picture (rouxl.es =IMAGE() or an embedded PNG) and 1-2 standard two-hand algs, 11 algs in all. 'Permutation' covers the 2 O cases: Adjacent Swap (O3) and Diagonal Swap (O6), with 2 algs each, 4 in all. The sheet has no prose, no names and no recognition tips; only the group numbers explain the structure. The algs are ordinary 2H algs, not OH-specific, despite the link text. Saved: CSV per tab, the xlsx, the htmlview, an all-tabs dump, and the 2 embedded images in 2look-media/.

resources.title: Derin's 1.5 Look CMLL Algorithms
resources.author: Derin Eryilmaz (Discord @derineryilmaz). The doc says it 'Used template from Kian's CMLLs' and links to Kian Mansour's CMLL doc.
resources.level: beginner to intermediate (a bridge for solvers who know 2-look CMLL but do not want to learn all 42 algs yet)
resources.summary: A single-tab Google Doc. The rouxcubing.com link text calls it 'Google Sheets', but it is a doc. It has 49 embedded case images in Kian's template style: top-view diagrams named U6.JPG, Pi1.JPG and so on. The intro defines 1.5-look CMLL for solvers who know 2-look (7 orientation + 2 permutation algs) and do not want to learn all 42 1-look algs. It says the solutions were generated by 'a simple program' from the author's alg preferences and may not be the most efficient. Method: each case is solved by an optional U move plus one of nine base algs (stage 1). This turns the case into one of seven pictured base cases, whose alg (stage 2) finishes CMLL. Stage 2 is shown in brackets, but the point is that only stage 1 must be memorised. The base table names the nine algs: X, XX, XXX (the F-sexy-F' family repeated 1-3 times), Sune, Stash, Sledge, AntiSune, AntiStash and AntiSledge. AntiStash and AntiSledge have no picture because they are used only as stage-1 moves. Then come 8 tables, one per OCLL group (O, H, Pi, U, T, S, As, L), covering all 42 cases. Each cell holds a case picture, the pattern name (e.g. Right Bar, Back Slash, Checkerboard, Columns, Rows; for L: Mirror, Inverse, Pure, Front Commutator, Diag, Back Commutator) and its stage-1 recipe with the stage 2 in brackets. 9 cases are solved outright by a single base alg plus AUF, so they are 1-look already. The other 33 need two steps; 2 cases list two alternatives. The case numbering and naming follow Kian's template, not Rouxles': for example U1 is 'Forward Slash' here but 'Front Row' in Anto's sheet. Saved: text export, HTML export, and the 49 extracted images in derin-15look-imgs/.

resources.title: Iuri's L CMLL Recog (browser title 'Iuri's L Recog')
resources.author: Recognition method by Iuri Grangeiro, 'originally posted in comments in RMS'; document written by Alex Friedman
resources.level: intermediate to advanced (full-CMLL users improving L-case recognition)
resources.summary: A short single-tab Google Doc subtitled 'works from every angle'. It has one embedded figure: the 6 L CMLL cases (Mirror, Inverse, Pure, Front Commutator, Diag, Back Commutator), each with blue arrows joining the stickers used for recognition. It defines two oriented corners. The pure corner has no U-colour side stickers next to it, and goes to UFR for the Pure case. The diag corner sits between the U-colour side stickers, and goes to UFR for the Diag case. The method sorts L cases by how the two top stickers relate: the same colour, opposite colours, or adjacent colours. Same: look for the opposite colour on an oriented corner's side. Its absence tells you where it is. The diag corner must be on R with the opposite colour on R, and the pure corner on L with the opposite colour on F/B. Opposite: the U-colour side stickers of the misoriented corners point toward the diag corner. Put it in UFR; its side matching a top colour gives the case. Adjacent: the oriented corner whose side colours match the two top colours goes to UFR, and whether it is the pure or the diag corner gives the case. The doc gives Iuri's original description, lightly edited. It covers doing only right-hand versions of the algs vs R/L mirrors, which Iuri thinks he uses in feet, and the claim that always looking at the same sticker locations keeps it fast. Alex's step-by-step paraphrase follows. It contains no algorithms. Saved: text export, HTML export, and the figure in lcmll-recog-imgs/.
